rationale: The contract pins the four numbered scope items and five acceptance criteria of #41, plus the two review follow-ups from #40 (IntervalHours validation, unknown categoryIds validation) called out explicitly in the task brief, and two robustness fixes requested in review of this PR (see REVIEW-3/REVIEW-4 below). Scheduling business logic is split into two focused Core.Services classes so each stays under the 5-constructor-parameter and 40-line method limits: JobSchedulingService (IJobStore, IScrapeStore, TimeProvider) owns 'queue one run per due, effectively-enabled job, skipping jobs with an active run' (scope 1-2, AC 'exactly one queued run' and 'not queued again'); ListingRefreshSchedulingService (IListingRefreshService, ISchedulerStateStore, TimeProvider, ScheduleOptions) owns 'run RefreshActiveListings once per refresh interval using a durably persisted last-run timestamp' (scope 3). Both take time from TimeProvider (scope 4), never real DateTime.UtcNow, so JobSchedulingServiceTests and ListingRefreshSchedulingServiceTests can simulate a process restart by constructing a second service instance against the same SQLite file with an advanced or unadvanced FakeTimeProvider and asserting persisted state (LastQueuedUtc on ScrapeJobs, LastListingRefreshUtc on the new SchedulerState table) prevents a premature re-run. IJobStore gains HasQueuedOrRunningRun(jobId) so JobSchedulingService can skip jobs with an active run without the scheduler doing its own querying; it was added to IJobStore rather than IScrapeStore (the initial plan) because ScrapeStore was already at the CI0004 ceiling of 10 public methods and #43 was concurrently modifying ScrapeStore/listing entities, so JobStore was both the analyzer-safe and merge-safe home; JobStoreTests is extended to cover it directly. IJobStore.MarkQueued now takes an explicit queuedUtc so the timestamp it persists always comes from the same TimeProvider the scheduler used to decide the job was due, rather than a fresh DateTime.UtcNow that could disagree with a faked clock; JobStoreTests is updated for the new signature. The scheduling worker was originally a single SchedulerWorker BackgroundService but was split into JobQueueingWorker and ListingRefreshWorker (two independent BackgroundServices, each ticking on its own Schedule:TickMinutes cadence) in response to review: a single loop meant a slow or blocked RefreshActiveListings (one HTTP fetch per active listing, tens of minutes to hours for a large listing set) starved job queueing of its 5-minute cadence for the whole loop iteration. As two separate hosted services, the .NET host runs their ExecuteAsync loops as independent tasks, so a long-running refresh no longer blocks queueing; JobQueueingWorkerTests and ListingRefreshWorkerTests cover each in isolation, and ListingRefreshWorkerTests::Should_let_job_queueing_proceed_while_a_refresh_is_still_in_progress proves the concurrency directly with a refresh stub blocked on a TaskCompletionSource. Each worker now also wraps its own scheduling call in its own try/catch (logging via ILogger, excluding OperationCanceledException, never rethrowing) rather than only the refresh step being protected as in the original single-worker design — on .NET's default BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost, an unhandled exception from either loop would previously have crashed the whole Etl host, taking the unrelated ScrapeWorker down with it. ListingRefreshSchedulingService.RefreshListingsIfDue was reordered to call ISchedulerStateStore.SetLastListingRefreshUtc before IListingRefreshService.RefreshActiveListings, so a failing refresh still durably records the attempt time and is not retried until the next full RefreshIntervalHours elapses, instead of hammering the scraper every tick when refresh keeps failing; ListingRefreshSchedulingServiceTests::Should_record_the_refresh_attempt_even_when_it_throws_and_not_retry_within_the_interval pins this. SchedulerQueuesJobsForScrapeWorkerTests is the AC-pinned end-to-end integration test: it creates a job through the real /api/jobs HTTP endpoint on a WebApplicationFactory<Program>, resolves IJobSchedulingService from that same DI container (with TimeProvider and IScrapeClient replaced via ConfigureServices — TimeProvider swapped for a FakeTimeProvider and IScrapeClient swapped for a canned-HTML stub, matching the pattern in RunPipelineUsesInProcessScraperTests), calls QueueDueJobs, then runs a real ScrapeWorker.RunOnce against the same IScrapeStore/IScrapeRunService resolved from the factory and asserts the run completed, the job's LastQueuedUtc reflects the fake clock, and the stubbed listing was persisted and is visible over GET /api/scrape/jobs/{id}/listings. This test is unaffected by the JobQueueingWorker/ListingRefreshWorker split since it exercises IJobSchedulingService and ScrapeWorker directly, not the BackgroundService wrapper. JobIntervalHoursValidationTests and JobCategoryValidationTests pin the two review follow-ups from #40: POST/PUT /api/jobs with IntervalHours < 1 returns 400 ValidationProblem instead of ever reaching the scheduler, and POST/PUT /api/jobs and POST /api/jobs/{id}/categories with an unknown categoryId return 400 ValidationProblem instead of the 500 SQLite FK failure that reaches the client today. At base every listed test is red: ISchedulerStateStore/IJobSchedulingService/IListingRefreshSchedulingService and IJobStore.HasQueuedOrRunningRun do not exist so the Core assembly does not compile, and the two validation checks are absent so the two validation test files fail (400 expected, 201/500 observed) once the assembly does compile. The migration was regenerated with `dotnet ef migrations add` after origin/main moved twice during implementation (#42/#43 merged first, touching ScrapeStore/listing entities and adding their own migration; #45 merged afterward, changing ISearchPageParser/ISearchPageService/ScrapeRunService/SearchPageService/ScrapeOptions shapes that this ticket's scope does not touch) so it orders after 20260923234122_AddListingDetailAndPriceHistory and the model snapshot stays consistent with all three changesets.
